result:
**The plan:** Plan 92 set out to bring the writing-skills meta-skill in line with the Claude Code guide. Eight claims (C1–C8) were wrong or missing. The worst were "always-resident" descriptions, an unsupported `@` force-load claim, and outdated fork advice. Claude Code facts were also mixed in with runtime-neutral advice. A stale `@2.1.219` citation left `cli.py lint` printing one STALE line, which would have blocked merges from 2026-11-27. The spec chose to distill, keep and refresh the TDD-for-docs deviation, waive reps for factual fixes, and review against main's guide.

**The build:** First came a micro-test kit with four frozen cases and isolated rep runs. Its pass rules and bars were fixed before any rep ran. A RED control on the old text came back null, since R1 passed everywhere. So no template slot was added, and S-67 closed on the record. Next, a new 64-line `references/claude-code.md` collected the frontmatter keys, the Haiku caveats, a guide-backed fork rule, and the listing and compaction limits. `discovery.md` and `SKILL.md` now point to it. The register dropped the gap and refreshed the deviation. Sixty new-layout reps met all 12 bars. A 56-row guide review fixed two contradicted rows, and the citation was restamped to eight sections at `@2.1.306`.

**The project:** The branch clears the STALE backlog and gives Claude Code facts one small home. It corrects the guidance that agents copy into new skills, and it closes three backlog items. Read-before-edit testing remains open, along with five new deferred items.
